text:
ana: noticed a sharp p99 latency spike on llama-3-13b after last infra roll (around seq=1800-2048). repro on ded-1 pool.

mike: ugh. gimme the perf dump pls, did allocator or kernel selector change in the deploy? :thinking_face:

ana: perf dump attached (trimmed). p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 120ms, p99 jumps to 980-1.2s for some requests. CPU % on host ok, GPU util stays ~60%.

ana: ```
# perf summary (requests at seq ~2000)
call_site:attention_fwd    time_ms: 12.4  calls: 256
call_site:kv_read         time_ms: 180.2 calls: 20   <- large
call_site:kv_write        time_ms: 2.1   calls: 256
call_site:mem_copy        time_ms: 430.1 calls: 2    <- big memcpy around cache flush
``` 

shiv: that kv_read jump smells like cache-evict thrash when we switch attention kernel (fused->split) for long seqs. any recent rope_theta/hidden-size mapping changes? maybe kernel selector swapped at seq threshold.

rachel: @ana can you run the micro-bench script on that model with --trace-kernel and --trace-kv to capture selector decisions? also include model config.

ana: running now. model config we use:

```
model_config:
  id: llama-3-13b
  hidden_size: "5120"
  num_heads: "40"
  rope_theta: "10000"
  activation: "silu"
  norm: "rmsnorm"
  kv_cache_policy: "lru-prefix-evict"
```

mike: hmm silu + rmsnorm + that head dim is an odd combo for our fused attention kernels. fused kernels assume contiguous qkv packing; RMSNorm change shouldn't by itself, but activation affects kernel memory working set.

ops-bot: deploy finished: infra/roll-2026-03-17 by @deploy-bot :rocket:

shiv: quick experiment: set kernel selector threshold to prefer fused_attn up to seq 2048 and increase dynamic_batching.pack_ratio to 0.85. also try kv_cache_policy: "sticky-prefix" to avoid evicting large prefixes.

ana: done. re-run synthetic load with packing enabled. prelim results: p99 down to ~220ms, memcpy spikes reduced. still occasional 480ms outliers.

mike: can you dump kernel_selector logs? what kernels triggered on the outliers?

ana: logs show fallback to split_attention on 3/200 calls (seq ~2024) with a memcopy of 380ms for key/val transpose.

rachel: maybe our split attention path does a naive transpose that thrashes cache for num_heads=40. try adding a small heuristic: if head_dim%32 !=0, prefer fused path even if seq>threshold.

mike: agree. implement in selector: prefer_fused_when_headdim_unaligned = true. Also add a safety cap on kv eviction: min_retained_prefix_tokens=1024.

shiv: also add a short-term metric: kv_read_latency.p99_by_seq_bucket so we can see exact boundary. create an alert if p99>500ms for any bucket.

ana: created alert, applied selector tweak in a canary on ded-1a. early telemetry shows p99 190-260ms and fewer evictions.

rachel: awesome. once canary is stable, roll to remaining pools and add unit test for kernel selector decisions (headdim/uncompressed vs seq).

mike: follow-up items: 1) patch selector + tests, 2) optimize split attention transpose for large heads, 3) evaluate sticky-prefix memory tradeoff on cost. I'll pick #2.

ana: thanks team. will open the PR and link perf logs. :thumbsup!
